statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Nasdaq and semiconductor weakness persists, but lower Treasury yields and oil leave downside confirmation incomplete.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold; the principal near-term risk window is the 18:00 UTC U.S. Treasury Iran-sanctions announcement and immediate post-event price discovery.
headline: Technology weakness keeps Nasdaq Tail risk at WATCH ahead of the sanctions event window
body: The Nasdaq is lower with semiconductor and megacap pressure, while Treasury yields and oil have declined. The mixed cross-asset picture keeps Tail at 24 despite extreme event stress. The 18:00 UTC Treasury sanctions announcement is the main near-term checkpoint; persistent one-way structure would require fresh observed confirmation.

forecast.analysis: Late Asia-hours conditions are expected to be calmer if cross-asset markets remain orderly. Tail would rise only if a new directional futures leg develops with confirming rates or energy stress.
Approaching Europe, the key checkpoint is whether overnight Nasdaq futures retain a range or begin a clean directional break. No such future break is assumed in advance.
The European open can reprice geopolitics and rates after thinner overnight trade. Stress edges higher, while Tail remains low unless the move becomes persistent and poorly retraced.
European follow-through is a confirmation window. Mixed sector and cross-asset behavior would keep Tail low; synchronized downside in tech, yields and volatility would be a stronger warning.
